name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd
about: Tata Consultancy Services is the flagship company and a part of Tata group. It is an IT services, consulting and business solutions organization that has been partnering with many of the world's largest businesses in their transformation journeys for over 50 years. TCS offers a consulting-led, cognitive powered, integrated portfolio of business, technology and engineering services and solutions. [1]

sections.one_liner: India's largest IT services firm; constant-currency growth near 3% and EBIT margin at 24% test its AI-led growth story.
business: IT services, consulting and engineering across 56 countries; 598,056 associates at Q2 FY27. [AR FY26] [Q1FY27 call]
Verticals: BFSI 38.7% (+9.3%), Communication/Media/Tech 15.9% (-14%), Consumer 14.8%, Life Sciences 10.4%, Manufacturing 10.2%, Others 10.0%. [AR FY26]
Geography: North America 48.6%, UK 17.4%, Continental Europe 15.4%, APAC 8.3%, India 5.9%, MEA 2.5%, LatAm 1.9%. [AR FY26]
Annualized AI revenue is $3.1B, over 10% of revenue, up from $1.8B in Q3 FY26. [Q1FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) revenue ₹73,188 cr, +11.2% YoY in rupees; constant currency only +2.8% YoY and +0.5% QoQ. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
TTM revenue ₹2,83,248 cr, EBITDA ₹74,916 cr (26.4%), PAT ₹51,858 cr. Q2 EBIT margin 24%, net margin 19%. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
ROCE 63%, ROE 51.8%, book value ₹329, so price/book is about 7.6x. [Numbers]
P/E 16.6x and dividend yield 2.56% at ₹2,503. Stock is 25% below its ₹3,350 high and 27% above its ₹1,976 low. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR slowed to 5.8% over 3 years from 10.2% over 5 years. PAT CAGR fell to 5.3% from 8.7%. [Numbers]
FY26 rupee revenue grew 4.6%, but constant currency fell 2.4%. Rupee weakness masks flat-to-down underlying demand. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
EBITDA margin stuck at 26–28% for six years. Quarterly OPM slipped from 27% to 26% in FY27 after wage hikes. [Numbers]
ROCE rose from 49% (FY21) to 65% (FY25), then 63% (FY26). The first dip coincides with acquisitions and data-centre spending. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings ₹11,808 cr against net worth ₹1,18,986 cr. D/E is 0.10, roughly flat from 0.09 in FY24. Effectively ungeared. [Numbers]
Debtor days rose from 67 (FY21) to 93 (FY26), while management cites 74-day DSO. The definition gap is not disclosed. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
HyperVault data centre costs ₹18,000 cr (TCS 51%, about ₹9,200 cr), roughly 2.2x FY26 capex of ₹4,081 cr. Expect internal funding. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 1.01 over 3 years. Q2 FY27 cash conversion was 102.2% of net income, versus 93% in Q1. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
FCF grew from ₹38,902 cr to ₹48,013 cr over FY23–26, about 7.3% CAGR, ahead of 5.3% PAT CAGR. [Numbers]
FY26 FCF was 97% of PAT. Net worth rose ₹11,746 cr in six months, suggesting lower payouts or retention for capex. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: AI revenue added about $1.3B annualized in three quarters, yet total constant-currency growth is 2.8% YoY. This implies non-AI revenue is shrinking. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
'Margin resilience' narrative versus EBIT: 25.3% in Q4 FY26, then 24% for two quarters. FY27 target already lowered to 'exit 25%+'. [Q1FY27 call]
Q2 PAT +14.9% YoY is a low-base effect. In Sep 2025, PAT fell QoQ while EBITDA rose 6.5%. Underlying growth is lower. [Numbers]
Dec 2025 PAT fell 13.9% YoY on flat margins. This is consistent with excluded charges: Labour Code ₹2,128 cr and restructuring ₹1,388 cr. [Numbers] [AR FY26]
guidance: Long-term margin aspiration of 26–28% is unchanged. Near term, growth investment comes ahead of margin recovery. [Q1FY27 call: Q2 FY27]
MHP acquisition expected to dilute EBIT margin by about 50bps in H2 FY27. [Q1FY27 call: Q2 FY27]
Target exit FY27 at a 25%+ operating margin, then progressively return to FY26 levels. [Q1FY27 call: Q1 FY27]
Data-centre revenue only starts 18–24 months after contract, so no near-term contribution from the ₹18,000 cr HyperVault. [Q1FY27 call: Q2 FY27] [AR FY26]
North America (2.4% YoY) expected to 'recover soon'. Q3 is seasonally strong for Consumer. No numeric targets given. [Q1FY27 call: Q2 FY27]

ledger.promised: Margin to inch toward 26–28% band; 25.2% at the time. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: EBIT 25.3% in Q4, then 24% in Q1/Q2 FY27; OPM fell from 27% to 26%. [Numbers]
FY26 TCV $40.7B with 5 mega deals (call figure; not in NUMBERS). [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.promised: Wage increments to hit margin by 150–200bps. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Wage hit 170bps; EBIT 24%, down 130bps; OPM fell from 27% to 26%. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: Positive FY27, stronger first half, international acceleration. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Dollar revenue flat QoQ in Q1, +0.5% constant currency in Q2; rupee QoQ +2.2%, +1.3%. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: Demand to improve in Q2 on pent-up backlog. [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Constant-currency QoQ only +0.5%; rupee QoQ slowed to 1.3% from 2.2%; India project deferred. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: Manufacturing to turn around in Q2. [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Manufacturing +3.1% QoQ constant currency (call figure; not in NUMBERS). [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.promised: Exit FY27 at a 25%+ operating margin. [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Q2 FY27 at 24%, with 50bps MHP dilution still to come in H2. [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.promised: MHP dilution of about 50bps on EBIT margin. [Q2FY27 call]

bull: FCF of ₹48,013 cr, CFO/PAT of 1.01 and D/E of 0.10 fund dividends (2.56% yield) plus capex internally. [Numbers]
TCV of $9.5–9.6B per quarter; FY26 TCV of $40.7B beat the $38–39B guide. Order book supports a growth pickup. [Q1FY27 call]
P/E of 16.6x with ROE of 51.8%. Stock is 25% below its high despite 63% ROCE. [Numbers]
bear: Constant-currency growth is about 3%. Rupee growth of 11–14% depends on currency and acquisitions; a rupee rally would expose it. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
Margin path keeps slipping: 26% aspiration, then 25.3%, then 24%, with 50bps MHP drag and 40% YoY subcontracting growth. [Q1FY27 call]
AI productivity pass-through of 10–15% deflates core revenue. Non-AI business appears to be shrinking. [Q1FY27 call]
questions: What is non-AI constant-currency revenue growth YoY, excluding MHP?
Why do reported debtor days (93) differ from your DSO (74)?
How much FY27–28 capex for HyperVault, and how does it affect payout ratio?
What subcontracting cost reduction is needed to exit FY27 at 25%?

guidance.quote: we're confident that growth momentum will continue

guidance.statement: North America recovery expected soon despite current growth lag; TCV and discussions remain strong.

themes: Enterprise AI adoption scaling from isolated use cases to governed agentic systems globally.
AI revenue $3.1B (10%+ total) becoming pervasive across all transformations, no substitution.
Demand selective, uneven; discretionary programs under scrutiny; medium-term momentum confident on pipeline strength.
Vendor consolidation and AI-powered engineering creating tailwinds in traditional service portfolios.
Prioritizing strategic investments in capacity, partnerships, acquisitions despite near-term margin headwinds.
Agentic control planes, AI governance, cost controls, security emerging as critical enterprise needs.
analyst_pushback: AI substitution vs incremental: Ruchi asked if cannibalization. Aarthi: AI pervasive, complementary across transformations.
India decline: Ravi flagged 10% drop, client metrics. Krithi: Project deferral, no structural issue, recovery expected.
Margin recovery path: Multiple analysts questioned 25% exit. Samir: Prioritizing growth, will inch up gradually.
North America weakness: Dipesh noted half company growth. Krithi: TCV strong, conversations good, recovery soon.

annual_report.business: Global IT services and consulting firm serving industry leaders across 56 countries with 580,000 employees. Provides AI, digital transformation, cloud, application development, engineering, cybersecurity services. Revenue from technology modernization projects, consulting, and managed services.

segments.name: Communication, Media and Technology
segments.comment: Declined 14% YoY from legacy deal completion

annual_report.revenue_mix: North America 48.6%, UK 17.4%, Continental Europe 15.4%, APAC 8.3%, India 5.9%, MEA 2.5%, Latin America 1.9%
strategy: Become world's largest AI-led technology services company
Build, Acquire, Partner across full AI stack infrastructure to intelligence
Drive internal transformation via Human+AI operating model
Build future-ready talent with 69 million annual learning hours
Expand AI ecosystem with 3,600 hyperscaler and OEM partnerships
annual_report.outlook: Global GDP 3.1% growth amid geopolitical uncertainty. Customers prioritizing AI adoption, cloud modernization, legacy transformation. Medium-term drivers: technology modernization, business transformation, operating model optimization through AI scaling.
annual_report.capex_plans: ₹18,000 crore HyperVault AI datacenter with TPG (51:49 split). Pan-India 50,000 seats expansion over 2-3 years. R&I ₹2,900 crore annually (1.1% revenue).
risks: Volatile geopolitical environment and macroeconomic uncertainty impacting client spending
Competitive pressure from deep-tech AI companies with platform-led solutions
Scaling gap between AI lab performance and enterprise implementations
Trade policy volatility and regional geopolitical tensions affecting growth
annual_report.flags: Exceptional items excluded: Labour Code impact ₹2,128 crore, CSC legal claim $112 million provision, restructuring termination benefits ₹1,388 crore.
